item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts did not mince his words when talking about Edwin Díaz during his mid-September rehab assignment. "He needs to pitch better. It hasn't been good," said Roberts.
Diaz, who has the highest average annual value in MLB relief pitcher history ($23M), struggled in the first four appearances of his rehab assignment. He had thrown just 40 of 86 pitches for strikes in his first four games with Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Diaz's fourth appearance was especially worrying. He threw 30 pitches — just 13 of them for strikes — walked three batters and allowed five runs. Diaz rehab came in the Pacific Coast League, which is notorious for being the most hitter-friendly league in all of baseball. That atrocious outing came in Sugar Land, however, which is the most pitcher-friendly venue in the PCL.
When the Dodgers activated Diaz from the injured list, Roberts revealed he'd be used in low-leverage situations. Well, he has been perfectly fine in his three low-leverage outings since September 18, which has assuaged some of the Dodgers fans panic levels.
Should Dodgers fans buy into Edwin Diaz’s success?
Diaz has only allowed one hit since returning from the IL. The Dodgers, however, had a run margin of +19 in those three games.
“The way he’s throwing, the ninth is possible, yes,” said Roberts after the Dodgers 7-0 win over the Padres on September 22.
The Dodgers will almost certainly give Diaz another opportunity against the San Diego Padres on Thursday. The current home series against the Friars will be Diaz's last opportunity to pitch against a playoff team before the postseason begins.
The Dodgers are currently without Emmet Sheehan, Edgardo Henriquez, Will Klein, and Eric Lauer. Outside of Alex Vesia, the rest of the bullpen is incredibly shaky. Tanner Scott has a 5.40 ERA so far this month, Justin Wrobleski has not improved since being moved to the bullpen, and who knows what Blake Treinen has left in the tank?
Dodgers fans should get accustomed to seeing Diaz the rest of the season. He's quite possibly the linchpin to this team going deep in the playoffs with the way this bullpen looks right now. Dodgers fans have the right to remain skeptical that Diaz will return to the optimal version of himself,

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Dodgers manager discusses intriguing postseason roster battle
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli

item.content:encoded:
Since being called up from Double-A Tulsa earlier this month as the corresponding move for Shohei Ohtani going on the 15-day injured list, Josue De Paula has done nothing but impress his Los Angeles Dodgers teammates and coaching staff.
The top prospect has flashed his elite offensive potential, showing remarkable plate discipline and power while drawing comparisons to New York Mets slugger Juan Soto.
With Ohtani returning from the IL on Wednesday, questions remain about De Paula’s role with the Dodgers moving forward. But the expectation is that he will compete with Dalton Rushing for the final spot on the team’s postseason roster.
“He’s done a great job,” manager Dave Roberts said of De Paula. “We made the move with Eliezer Alfonzo out on option with Andy (Pages) coming back. With Shohei coming back, I’m just not sure what the counter is going to be. But to your question, Josue has done a fantastic job.”
Rushing has been on the 10-day injured list since Sept. 6 after re-aggravating his right elbow while playing catch. However, he took live batting practice against Will Klein on Tuesday and should be activated in the coming days.
That would give Rushing only a few games to show the Dodgers he is back up to game speed and deserving of a spot on their postseason roster.
“Dalton, taking his at-bats. The thought is to give him an opportunity at some point in time to get activated and see how it looks coming off the bench,” Roberts said. “So I’m not sure if that’s tomorrow, Thursday, Friday, something like that.”
Rushing was in the midst of a breakout season before the right elbow injury threw him off course, so it will be interesting to see which direction the Dodgers decide to take.
Dodgers postseason roster battle
The Dodgers will consider several factors when choosing between De Paula and Rushing for the final spot on their postseason roster, including the ability to put together a good at-bat, not chasing pitches out of the strike zone and power.
“Quality of at-bat, conducting an at-bat, the ability to swing at strikes, take balls, get on base, get a hit,” Roberts explained. “There’s potential slug with both those guys. It’s going to be a good debate.
“I think hitting off the bench is very difficult, and you’re just trying to figure out who gives us the best chance. To be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time that he’s missed. To kind of think that you have three games to get back into playoff form, it’s tough to do. It’s not a knock on him. He’s been great for us, but it’s still tough.
“And also when you’re talking about having the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. But again, we have to have those conversations and make a decision.”

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — It’s the final week of the regular season and the Dodgers are sorting things out as they prepare for the postseason, which they hope will start on October 3 in the National League Division Series rather than September 29 in the wild card round.
Before Tuesday’s game, Blake Snell pitched a bullpen session at Dodger Stadium as he works his way back from leaving last Wednesday’s start with left groin discomfort. Manager Dave Roberts said Snell is in line to start on Saturday in San Francisco against the Giants, with Tarik Skubal — currently on the bereavement list — starting Friday night at Oracle Park.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto starts Wednesday and Tyler Glasnow Thursday against the Padres.
Also on Tuesday, reliever Will Klein pitched a simulated inning against Dalton Rushing in a battle of players on the injured list. Klein is on the 60-day injured list with elbow discomfort and not eligible to be activated until September 30 at the earliest, but it looks like he’ll be in the stay-hot camp should the Dodgers have room to add him at some point later in the postseason, similar to in 2025 when Klein wasn’t active until the World Series and he pitched five scoreless innings, including four innings in the marathon Game 3.
“With Will it’s more get healthy, show that you’re healthy, throw to some hitters,” Roberts said. “He’ll throw during the week off, then we’ll kind of see if there’s an opportunity later on in the postseason, sort of like last year.”
Rushing is trying to work his way back from elbow discomfort suffered when practicing throwing. His role would be a left-handed bat off the bench, a role currently occupied by Josue De Paula, who has been the designated hitter with Shohei Ohtani out. But Ohtani is expected to be activated Wednesday barring an unforeseen setback.
That essentially sets up a battle between Rushing and De Paula for a postseason roster spot, though Roberts said the plan is to activate Rushing at some point this week to literally get back into the swing of things.
“Quality of at-bat, conducting an at-bat obviously, the ability to swing at strikes, take balls, get on base, get a hit. There’s potential slug with both guys. I think it’s a good debate,” Roberts said. “Hitting off the bench is very difficult so we’re trying to figure out who gives us the best chance.
“And to be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time he’s missed, and to think that you have [three] games to get back into playoff form, it’s tough to do. It’s not a knock on him, he’s been great for us, but it’s still tough, right, Given that we talk about having the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. But we have to have those conversations and make a decision.”
Activating both Ohtani and Rushing this week, when the Dodgers have 14 active position players, would require two corresponding moves to make room on the active roster. If De Paula doesn’t get sent down — “I think Josue has done a fantastic job,” Roberts said Tuesday — that might mean rough news for Alexes Call and Freeland, either this week or next.

item.content:encoded:
Entering the final week of the regular season, the Dodgers more or less know their postseason fate.
They've locked up the National League West. They are a seemingly safe four games clear of the Atlanta Braves for a first-round bye. And, unless they can close a two-game gap on the Milwaukee Brewers without holding the tiebreaker, they will finish as the NL's No. 2 seed, getting home-field advantage at least for the NL Division Series.
Thus, the real intrigue for now is who might be on the Dodgers' postseason roster when the playoffs begin next month.
This year, injuries and fluctuating performances have forced them to cycle 53 different players through their clubhouse.
And while the core of the group is clear, many questions remain about how the club will construct its lineup and pitching staff for this fall's pursuit of a third-straight World Series.
Here is the California Post's best guess about how it will all shake out.
Lineup locks
Will Smith, Freddie Freeman, Tommy Edman, Mookie Betts, Max Muncy, Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages, Kyle Tucker, Shohei Ohtani, Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia
There won't be any big surprises in how the Dodgers line up to begin the playoffs, assuming Ohtani is healthy enough to resume everyday DH'ing duties.
Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker have cemented their place as everyday hitters thanks to late-season surges. Andy Pages is due back on Tuesday from a fractured hand. Freddie Freeman still seems somewhat limited by his right knee injury, but has nonetheless been able to manage it well enough to this point. And while Tommy Edman has been slumping lately, he doesn't seem to be in immediate danger of losing at-bats.
On the bench, Hunter Feduccia has locked up the back-up catching job, and could be a left-handed hitting option as a pinch-hitter. Kiké Hernández and Miguel Rojas, meanwhile, each provide versatile defensive depth, as well as extensive track records for postseason heroics when called upon.
Entering the final week of the regular season, the core of the Dodgers' position player group looks as they expected.
Dodgers Lineup questions
Bubble candidates: Josue De Paula, Dalton Rushing, Alex Call, Alex Freeland, Hyeseong Kim
The Dodgers will still have one, if not two, position player spots to fill depending on how they construct their roster (i.e. an even 13 pitchers/13 hitters, or a 12/14 split like they used last year?)
And for those, they could have a number of difficult decisions.
First and foremost: Will Josue De Paula make the playoff roster?
If he does, it will likely be as a left-handed bench bat; though if there is any lingering uncertainty with Ohtani, he could also provide insurance as a backup DH option. His main competition right now figures to be Alex Call (who might be redundant to Rojas and Hernández as a right-handed bench bat) or Dalton Rushing (who is an intriguing alternative as a left-handed bat, but remains sidelined from the setback he suffered with his elbow injury earlier this month).
In just 10 MLB games, De Paula has quickly built a strong case, showing supreme plate discipline (10 walks to only four strikeouts) and the potential for power (three doubles, one home run, seven RBIs). At this point, it might be more of a surprise if he doesn't make it.
If the Dodgers elect to carry an extra position player on top of that, the choices are even more varied.
Last year, they rostered two base-running/defensive specialists throughout the playoffs in infielder Hyeseong Kim and outfielder Justin Dean. Dean is now gone, and Hernández could serve as a late-game defensive outfield replacement anyway. But Kim remains in consideration, manager Dave Roberts said, thanks to his speed and infield glove. Alex Freeland could also factor in here, as someone capable of providing more at the plate.
Lineup projection for Los Angeles
C: Will Smith
1B: Freddie Freeman
2B: Tommy Edman
SS: Mookie Betts
3B: Max Muncy
LF: Teoscar Hernández
CF: Andy Pages
RF: Kyle Tucker
DH: Shohei Ohtani
Bench: Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia, Josue De Paula, Hyeseong Kim*
*If the Dodgers carry 14 position players
Dodgers pitching staff locks
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips
The Dodgers' starting rotation is set, assuming no further setbacks with Blake Snell's groin injury. The back end of the bullpen has come into focus, too, with Tanner Scott and/or Roki Sasaki the most logical candidates to serve as closer, and Alex Vesia and Evan Phillips separating themselves as the team's next most-trusted high-leverage relief options.
The only real question here is how the Dodgers will line up the rotation. Yamamoto-Skubal would make sense for Games 1 and 2 of a division series (keeping them both on-line for a potential Game 5). But could Tyler Glasnow's potential issues with traveling tempt the Dodgers to use him primarily at home, if they can? All factors to consider in the coming weeks.
Pitching staff questions
Roster bubble candidates: Brock Stewart, Edwin Díaz, Blake Treinen, Kris Bubic, Jack Dreyer, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski, Edgardo Henriquez, Will Klein, Eric Lauer
The first thing the Dodgers need to figure out here is health.
Edgardo Henriquez will almost certainly be on the playoff roster, and pitching in a high-leverage role, if he can make a full recovery from his recent back strain. Will Klein and Eric Lauer might also be available health-wise, though lack clear roles to step immediately back into.
Otherwise, the Dodgers will effectively have at least four open spots for six to seven other pitchers.
For added right-handed depth, they might be deciding between Brock Stewart (who has been a go-to weapon against right-handed hitters recently), Edwin Díaz (who is trying to salvage his dismal debut season, and did throw a pair of scoreless outings this weekend) and Blake Treinen (who has curiously pitched only five times in three weeks since being activated from the injured list, and not in the highest of leverage).
For another left-handed option, they could go with Kris Bubic (the trade deadline acquisition who has impressed with three scoreless appearances since returning from an injury) or Jack Dreyer (who was one of the Dodgers' best relievers from June to August, but has given up five runs in his last seven outings).
And for a multi-inning role, they will have Emmet Sheehan (who has looked like a different pitcher in three sterling starts since returning from a minor-league demotion) and Justin Wrobleski (the breakout All-Star who has finally shaken some of his home run problems since moving to the bullpen).
There are many permutations that the Dodgers could employ depending on opponent. They're still figuring out the exact hierarchy of all their bullpen arms, too.
But as long as their rotation is dominant, everything else should take care of itself.
Pitching staff projection
Rotation: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow
Bullpen: Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Kris Bubic, Edwin Díaz, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched their 13th National League West title in the last 14 seasons, and now all that remains to do is stay in front of the Atlanta Braves down the stretch to secure a first-round bye.
“It’s always helpful in the sense of giving your guys a break to reset. But given all the tax and where our guys are health-wise, to get that week would be huge,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts recently said. “We’ve still got to play well to finish out the season to get to that point. There’s a lot of people that could use the break.”
The Dodgers have a four-game lead over the Braves for the second seed in the NL. L.A. needs to finish with a better record than the Braves by virtue of not holding the head-to-head tiebreaker.
The top seed in the NL is within reach for the Dodgers, but they do not control their own destiny due to trailing the Milwaukee Brewers in the standings. Furthermore, the Dodgers also don’t have the tiebreaker over the Brewers.
Securing home-field advantage throughout the postseason would certainly be of value, but finishing as one of the top two division winners in the NL is of greater importance.
Some of the notable injuries the Dodgers are dealing with include Shohei Ohtani, Edgardo Henriquez, Andy Pages, Will Klein and, most recently, Blake Snell.
The Wild Card Series begins Tuesday, Sept. 29, while the NL Division Series starts Saturday, Oct. 3.
Pages and Ohtani are expected to be activated prior to the regular season concluding, and there is optimism Snell will avoid going on the injured list.
Henriquez is eligible to return on the same day the Wild Card round begins. Meanwhile, Klein can’t return until the NLDS starts. It is not a given that the Dodgers would elect to have Klein on their postseason roster given his two-month absence, but they would still prefer to have the option.
Dodgers postseason outlook
Should the Dodgers remain the No. 2 seed in the NL postseason bracket, they would face the Wild Card winner of the matchup between the third division champion and sixth-place team. However, who that could be is still very much in question in part because of a late surge from the San Diego Padres.
The Chicago Cubs, Philadelphia Phillies and Padres are all in a dead heat and mathematically possible of slotting into any order as the three Wild Card teams.

item.content:encoded:
This is your one-stop shop for every Dodgers stint on the injured list during the 2026 season. We’ll also include every time a player misses time on the paternity list, bereavement leave, or is on the family medical emergency list as well.
Basically any time a player misses time that requires a roster move, we’ll note it here.
During the 2025 season, 28 different Dodgers players spent time on the injured list, some of them for multiple stints. That matched the team total from 2024, while in 2023 the Dodgers saw 34 players miss time on the IL.
Every injured-list stint is a transaction and will also be chronicled on our 40-man roster page. Both are essentially living documents that will be constantly updated throughout the season as these moves happen.
Injured-list stints for pitchers are a minimum of 15 days, and for position players it’s at least 10 days.
During spring training, the Dodgers placed both Evan Phillips and Kiké Hernández on the 60-day injured list, which opened up space on the 40-man roster for other moves. On opening day, six more Dodgers were placed on the injured list, including Blake Snell and Tommy Edman.
For more information on each specific injured list stint, click on the links on the dates in the list below this table.
